_what: The identity-handle ablation: each catalogue's profiles regenerated with the item's identifying fields withheld, to test whether a profile is a function of the metadata the pipeline ships or of what the model already knows. MEASURED on 2026-09-03; every field records how.
_design: Withheld: the structured identity fields (Steam - title, developer, publisher; ML-20M - title, year, director, cast, and the genres, which share the prompt's title line and went with it). Kept: every other field (Steam - tags, genres, specs; ML-20M - the plot, keywords, genome tags, scores and user tags). The two masks are therefore not matched: Steam kept its genres.
_caveat: A STRUCTURED-handle ablation. ML-20M free text still leaks identity - the plot names characters, and user tags carry actor names - so the ML-20M figure means 'the title is redundant when the description already determines the profile', NOT 'the model uses no recall'. Do not report it as a recall estimate.
_method: Both arms encoded with bge-large-en-v1.5 (the paper's encoder). Retrieval = each masked profile ranked against the full profiles of the same paired items (candidates_per_query).
_sample: The first 1,000 items of each catalogue by identifier (movieIds 1-1116 on ML-20M; the lowest Steam app ids), not a random sample: both lean towards their catalogue's older titles.
_recompute: tools/identity_retrieval.py FULL MASKED recomputes every figure here from the two arms' profile files (not released). background_cosine is the mean cosine between a masked profile and the other paired items' full profiles (0.658 and 0.687).
_payload_basis: prompt_payload_tokens is the median item payload in characters / 3.8, on the same basis in both catalogues: Steam's is its joined title, genres, tags, specs, developer and publisher (tools/recon_steam.py); MovieLens's is the rendered user prompt minus the template's literal text (median 1,624 - 238 = 1,386 characters, from the data repository's metadata/prompt_manifest.jsonl and USER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE in src/profile_generator/config/settings.py). Neither includes the system prompt, which is billed on every call: billed_input_tokens (2,012 on MovieLens, src/generation_economics.json) is the total input per profile, 1,389 of it the system prompt. Characters / 3.8 undercounts MovieLens's text, which carries numbers and tag lists: the live 5-item re-run billed 2,043.8 input tokens per profile, 1,389 of them system prompt, about 2.65 characters a token on those prompts, which would put the median payload near 520 tokens. Steam's ratio was not measured. The comparison holds on either estimator.

steam._why_998_not_1000: 1,000 games were attempted in both arms. Two produced no MASKED profile at all: with the identity withheld, 'Hot Dish' has genres none / tags ['Casual'] / specs ['Single-player'] and 'Mightier' has genres ['Indie'] / tags ['Indie'] / specs ['Single-player','Game demo'], and the model declined to write an 80-120 word profile from that, replying that the input was insufficient. Both generated normally in the FULL arm. This is the boundary condition at its limit -- not an error to retry past -- so the pair count is 998 and the two refusals are reported rather than coerced.
steam._identifier_repair: The Steam parser overwrites the identifier with the catalogue's own before parsing, as the movie pipeline does: the model can emit an unquoted identifier built from the title ('"itemId": 40k_dow2_cr' for Warhammer 40,000), the same property documented for the movie catalogue ('34street1994'), which would otherwise fail to parse.

ml20m._note: the full arm is the released catalogue; only the masked arm was generated

candidates_per_query: the paired set of the same catalogue (998 on Steam, 1,000 on MovieLens 20M)
